news.title: Sonia Bompastor delivers injury update on Blues quartet
news.body_en: Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor has provided updates on the fitness of Nathalie Bjorn, Erin (Cuthbert), Manaka Matsukubo and Mayra Ramirez ahead of our UEFA Women's Champions League third qualifying round second leg against Real Sociedad. A place in the league phase of the competition can be secured tomorrow evening at the Estadio Zubieta, and the Blues have travelled to the Basque Country with a commanding 5-2 advantage after the first leg at Plough Lane last week. Tomorrow's second leg will be broadcast live and for free on the Chelsea Official App and website, and begins at 7pm local time (6pm in the UK). Bompastor will be back in the Blues dugout after serving a one-match suspension last week, and ahead of the game in Spain, she delivered the latest team news and outlined the mentality with which her side must approach the game. 'The update for this game is that Erin (Cuthbert), Nat (Nathalie Bjorn), Mayra (Ramirez) and Manaka (Matsukubo) are not available,' she said. 'I think for us, we need to approach the game as if it were 0-0. I have enough experience in football to know anything can happen. 'We have a really good team, and the only thing that will stop us from achieving our goal is if we become complacent and we don't approach the game with the right mindset. 'I think that's what makes the difference between the best teams and the good teams. For me, that's really important, and I will probably mention something to the players before the game tomorrow.' This Saturday, Chelsea will play at Stamford Bridge for the first time since it became our permanent home. Welcome the Blues by securing your ticket for our first WSL clash of the season against Aston Villa now!

news.title: Mykhailo Mudryk completes season-long loan switch
news.body_en: Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk has joined Tottenham Hotspur on a season-long loan. Signed from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023, the Ukraine international has made 73 appearances for the Blues and scored ten goals. Mudryk helped the Blues reach the Carabao Cup final during his first full season at the club and featured en route to our UEFA Conference League triumph. We look forward to monitoring and supporting Misha throughout his time at Spurs.

news.title: Dujuan Richards seals loan switch
news.body_en: Chelsea forward Dujuan Richards has joined League One side AFC Wimbledon on a season-long loan. Signing for the Blues in January 2024, Richards scored seven goals in 10 games for our Under-21s during the second half of that season. Having been sidelined due to injury during the following campaign, the Jamaica international returned to action with our Under-21s and spent the second half of last season on loan at Leicester City in the Championship. We look forward to supporting Dujuan throughout his loan with the Dons.

news.title: Robert Sanchez departs on loan
news.body_en: Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has completed a season-long loan move to Serie A side Como. Sanchez arrived at Stamford Bridge from Brighton and Hove in August 2023 and has made 112 appearances for the Blues. The 28-year-old was part of the Chelsea squad that won the UEFA Conference League and the FIFA Club World Cup. We look forward to supporting Rob throughout his time in Italy.

news.title: Dario Essugo completes loan switch
news.body_en: Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo has completed a season-long loan move to RC Strasbourg.   Arriving at Stamford Bridge from Sporting CP in June 2025 ahead of the FIFA Club World Cup, Essugo featured three times during the tournament as the Blues were crowned world champions. We look forward to supporting Dario throughout his loan in France.

news.title: Chelsea Women travelling squad confirmed for Real Sociedad
news.body_en: A 21-player Chelsea squad has been confirmed for the return leg of our Women's Champions League qualifier away to Real Sociedad. The Blues head into Wednesday's second leg with a 5-2 advantage secured at Plough Lane last week and, following that clash, Sociedad head coach Arturo Ruiz left the Spanish side to join Brighton & Hove Albion in the Women's Super League. Tomorrow's match, held at the Estadio Zubieta in San Sebastian, will kick off at 7pm local time, which will be 6pm in the UK. The game will be shown live on the Chelsea Official App and website. You just need to make sure you are signed in! news.title: Deivid Washington completes permanent transfer
news.body_en: Deivid Washington has completed a permanent transfer to RC Strasbourg.   The 21-year-old joined the Blues in August 2023 from Santos and made three first-team appearances during his debut campaign. Having featured regularly for our Under-21s during the first half of the following season, he returned to Santos on loan in February 2025 and made 20 appearances for the Brazilian club. We thank Deivid for his efforts throughout his time at Chelsea and wish him well as he begins a new chapter in his career.

On the men's side, we will start to look ahead to the big London derby with Arsenal. Xabi Alonso will be sitting down at Cobham to speak to the gathered media in his pre-match press conference to preview our trip to Arsenal. You can watch it live on the Chelsea Official App and website, or catch up on demand later in the day. Chelsea Women are switching their focus from Europe back to domestic matters for the weekend, starting with Bompastor's pre-match press conference to preview our Women's Super League meeting with Aston Villa. That will take place at Cobham at 3pm on Friday and you can watch it live on the Chelsea Official App and website, or catch up on demand afterwards. The game will be live on Sky Sports in the UK and you can follow all the build-up, action and reaction - plus live commentary - as it happens in our Arsenal vs Chelsea Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and website. news.title: Real Sociedad vs Chelsea Women: How to watch, kick-off time, live stream info
news.body_en: Chelsea Women are looking to finish the job and book our place in the league phase of the UEFA Women's Champions League when we travel to Spain. The Blues are facing the Spanish side in a two-legged qualifying play-off in our bid to reach the league phase of this season's European competition, following our third-place finish in the Women's Super League in the previous campaign. Chelsea made a good start, with a 5-2 win in our first match at Plough Lane giving us a healthy lead to defend when the two sides meet again in San Sebastian. Here is everything you need to know about how to watch Chelsea Women against Real Sociedad, including kick-off time and how to follow the action on official Chelsea channels. Chelsea Women's game against Real Sociedad takes place on Wednesday 2 September 2026 at the Estadio Izan, with kick-off scheduled for 6pm UK time. You can watch the second leg of our Women's Champions League qualifier against Real Sociedad for free on the Chelsea Official App and Chelsea website. As always, team news, live updates and match coverage will be provided in our Real Sociedad vs Chelsea Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and Chelsea website. You can also follow Chelsea Women’s social media channels on X, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. Chelsea have a 100 per cent record this term. We won both of our pre-season friendlies - the 7-0 success against Auckland in New Zealand as followed up by a 3-0 victory over an A-League All-Stars side in Sydney - before opening the competitive action with that 5-2 first-leg win over Real Sociedad. Since last week's first leg, our Spanish opponents opened their Primera Division campaign with a 2-0 home loss to Logrono on Saturday, meaning they have started their season with back-to-back defeats, after last term's third-place league finish. The first-leg meeting at Plough Lane was the first-ever match between the two sides. The Blues had to come from behind after Ainhoa Marin gave Sociedad an early lead, but Naomi Girma soon headed us level from a corner. Veerle Buurman gave Chelsea the lead after the break, but this time the Spaniards hit back through Cecilia Marcos. We finally pulled clear during the final 25 minutes, though, as a brace by debutant Melvine Malard - either side of Lauren James' strike - gave us a healthy three-goal lead to take into the second game. Be there to welcome CFCW to our new Women's Super League home at Stamford Bridge when we take on Aston Villa in our first WSL match of the season on 5 September at 12.35pm!

news.title: Transfer deadline day 2026: Everything you need to know
news.body_en: Transfer Deadline Day has arrived. Here are the key dates, timings and regulations as the summer window draws to a close, plus a recap of Chelsea’s business so far. The 2026 summer transfer window in England closes at 11pm UK time on Tuesday 1 September 2026. The window, which opened on Monday 15 June, has returned to the traditional 11pm deadline following last summer’s earlier finish. The major European leagues also close their windows on Tuesday 1 September. Clubs in the Bundesliga, Serie A and Ligue 1 have until 7pm UK time to complete their business. The window in Spain remains open until 11pm UK time. Players can still leave English clubs after the Premier League window shuts if the destination country’s registration period remains open. Clubs in the Netherlands and Major League Soccer can sign players until Wednesday 2 September. The Scottish window closes at 5pm on Thursday 3 September, with Austria and Belgium also open that day. The deadline in Turkey is Friday 4 September, while clubs in Mexico have until 11 September and those in Portugal until 15 September. The Saudi Arabian window remains open until 12 October. Unattached players can also be signed after the deadline, subject to the relevant competition’s registration and squad-list rules. If two clubs reach an agreement shortly before 11pm, they can submit a deal sheet to the Premier League confirming the transfer. That provides an additional two hours to complete and submit the remaining documentation. As a result, transfers may still be formally completed or announced after the window has closed. Premier League clubs can make unrestricted changes to their squad lists while the transfer window remains open. After the deadline, each club submits a squad containing no more than 25 senior players. No more than 17 of those players can be non-homegrown, with the remaining places reserved for homegrown players. A homegrown player, irrespective of nationality, is somebody who was registered with a club affiliated to the Football Association or Football Association of Wales for three entire seasons or 36 months before turning 21, or before the end of the season in which they turned 21. Players under-21 do not count towards the 25-player limit and remain eligible to play in the Premier League. For the 2026/27 season, that applies to players born on or after 1 January 2005. Marco Palestra became our first recruit of the summer, arriving from Atalanta at the beginning of July. Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha also officially joined the Blues following agreements reached in previous windows. Morgan Rogers completed a move from Aston Villa and Maxence Lacroix made the short journey across London from Crystal Palace. Danny Welbeck joined from Brighton and Hove Albion, while Jordan Henderson arrived after leaving Brentford. Further additions included Valentin Barco from Strasbourg, Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano and World Cup-winning goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa. Dastan Satpayev completed his transfer following his 18th birthday before joining Burnley on loan for the season. Youngsters Harrison Bettoni and Alfie Osborne also arrived from Wigan Athletic and Hearts, respectively.

news.title: Analysis: Flying wingers, why possession isn't always king and Joao Pedro at it again
news.body_en: This was a different Chelsea than we have been accustomed to over the years, but it was definitely effective. We look at how Xabi Alonso masterminded the Blues' 4-3 win over Brighton & Hove Albion. With 14 goals in our first three games this season, it's fair to say life under Alonso has been exciting so far. Chelsea raced to a 3-0 lead against Brighton at Stamford Bridge, courtesy of goals from Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro. Brighton reduced the deficit to 3-2 before a moment of pure class from the rejuvenated Cole Palmer meant the Seagulls' 90+6-minute header was a mere consolation. Here we take a look at how the game was won... It is often said, 'Possession is king' when the importance of dominating the ball in modern football comes up in conversation. On Saturday, Chelsea proved that isn't always the case. Our 4-3 victory over Brighton saw the Blues have just 26 per cent possession across the 90 minutes, with our 225 passes attempted and 152 passes completed Chelsea's lowest figures since Opta records began during the 2003/24 season. But this wasn't a case where the Blues were under the kosh throughout or where the stats were skewed based on a second-half onslaught; our possession was at 30 per cent at half-time when we enjoyed a 3-1 lead. This was a calculated game plan from new manager Xabi Alonso, and it worked. The 'xG race' graphic below shows how each team's cumulative expected goals (xG) total builds throughout a match. The chart tracks the quality of chances created over time, rather than just the actual scoreline, with a steep rise highlighting a high-quality chance. The graphic highlights how the Blues were good value for their 3-0 lead because of the quality of chances they created. These were not pot-shots from distance which fortuitously came off; all three finishes came within ten yards of the Brighton goal. Alonso decided he would allow Brighton to have more of the ball and would then look to utilise our counter-attacking threat and the outstanding quality of our front three in the final third. When Sky Sports revealed the Blues had enjoyed less than a third of possession during the first half, it would have come as a shock to many because the hosts had clearly been the better team and had carried the greater threat. Alonso acknowledged post-match that after a 'brilliant first half an hour', his team 'played too much with the result in mind' and were too deep at times but understandably highlighted they are still in a process of improvement, with this just his third competitive game in charge of the Blues. But across the whole 90 minutes, Chelsea were good value for the win and the tactical plan paid off. Chelsea's directness was clear from the off and was backed up by the statistics post-match. The Blues utilised the forward passing ability of their deeper players, the speed of their wing-backs and the power and pace of Joao Pedro up top to great effect as we regularly got up the field quickly. The fact Emi Martinez made the second-highest 'completed passes in the opposition third', just one behind Morgan Rogers and level with Joao Pedro, shows just how much the Blues looked to go from back to front with speed. Based on Opta data, new goalkeeper Martinez only made one short pass from his 38 passes, meaning 97.4 per cent of his deliveries were considered 'long passes'. Only Mark Schwarzer against Liverpool in 2014 has a higher percentage (100 per cent from 31) for Chelsea since Opta started collecting data in 2003/04. Petr Cech was the other to go above 97 per cent on three occasions. This wasn't a goalkeeper just hitting and hoping, though; Martinez was regularly picking out the runs of players like Joao Pedro and Pedro Neto. Martinez passing to Joao Pedro was the most used combination between any Chelsea players, with eight. And, according to Opta, Martinez became just the second Chelsea goalkeeper to create two or more clear chances in a Premier League game since they started collecting data, with Robert Sanchez also providing two against the same opposition last season. Only Wayne Hennessy has ever created more, with three for Burnley against Manchester United in December 2021. The decision to go direct would have been influenced by the fact Alonso had the option of playing one of the fastest players in the Premier League in Pedro Neto - he recorded the eighth quickest time for the whole of the 2025/26 campaign at 22.6 miles per hour. And Jorrel Hato has already shown this season he is no slouch either. Despite lining up as wing-backs in the static formation graphic, and often being deep in our half when defending against Brighton attacks, Neto was often one of our most advanced players and Hato, although seen as a defender by trade, was a real attacking threat, too. It was Neto's cross from the byline which won the corner that ultimately led to Romeo Lavia's opening goal - a set-piece he also delivered. The Portugal international then ran from close to 30 yards out to get on the end of Morgan Rogers' cross for the second goal, and probably would have scored the third, had Joao Pedro not got to the ball first. That third goal was indicative of the two wing-backs' attacking threat throughout the game. They were both inside the Chelsea penalty area when Hato started the move. The Netherlands international then ran almost the length of the pitch before sliding the ball into the box. Neto had matched Hato stride for stride on the opposite side of the pitch and was there ready to collect the pass, had Joao Pedro not controlled and finished expertly. With Marco Palestra - the player judged to be the quickest in the Serie A last season - still to return from injury, one suspects this won't be the last time we see Chelsea wing-backs' pace posing a counter-attacking threat this season. Joao Pedro appears to be getting better and better every week. The forward made an immediate impact at Chelsea, finishing the season with 20 goals in all competitions and claiming the club's Player of the Season Award. But with the creative talents of Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers behind him, the Brazilian appears to have gone up another level. On Saturday, Joao scored one and set up another. In truth, he probably should have scored twice, as he uncharacteristically shot wide from inside the penalty area. But it isn't just the goal contributions that make him special. It is his all-round play. It's the game-high figure of 13 duels that he won, it's the work rate he showed out of possession, it's every part of his game. Chelsea have a special forward on their hands and fans will be excited to see the level he can reach over the coming years.

news.title: David Fofana completes permanent move
news.body_en: David Fofana has completed a permanent transfer to Swiss Super League side Servette.  The 23-year-old signed for the Blues from Molde in January 2023, scoring 17 goals and providing three assists during his time at Chelsea and on loan. We thank David for his efforts during his time at Chelsea and wish him well as he begins a new chapter in his career.

news.title: PL2 report: Chelsea Cobham Next Gen 5-4 West Ham United U21s
news.body_en: An incredible afternoon of drama saw Chelsea Cobham Next Gen come from three goals down to equalise, go behind once more and still manage to come back to secure a memorable 5-4 victory over London rivals West Ham United in the final minutes of the game. West Ham striker Josh Landers will go home knowing he couldn't have done much more to secure victory for the Hammer, as he completed a first-half hat-trick for the visitors to put his side 3-0 up and then grabbed another in the second period. However, Harrison Bettoni's goal in first-half injury-time proved critical for the Blues as we mounted a second-half fightback. Lewi Richards and Sol Gordon both scored superb - albeit very different - goals to bring the Blues level before Landers restored West Ham’s advantage with his fourth goal. But with just two minutes of normal time remaining, Reggie Watson made it two penalties in as many PL2 games when he converted and in the second minute of injury-time, Chizaram Ezenwata lifted the ball over the goalkeeper to complete a memorable comeback. It was Chelsea who applied the early pressure. The first opening fell to Leo Black, whose left-footed drive from distance was blocked, before Ezenwata worked space in the box but his right-footed effort was charged down. But the visitors went ahead after 13 minutes. Ryan Battrum’s header was not collected and Landers reacted to bundle the ball in. Chelsea looked to bounce back initially. Bettoni missed with a close-range header, Olutayo Subuloye saw his follow-up blocked, Sol Gordon saw a header saved, as did Richards with his two efforts. Landers doubled West Ham’s advantage in ten minutes before the break, meeting Junior Robinson’s cross from the right and finding the net from close range. A third followed seven minutes later. Jethro Medine delivered from the left and Landers was left with a simple finish into an empty net to complete his hat-trick. Chelsea grabbed a crucial lifeline in the third minute of first-half stoppage time. Richards curled a cross into the box from the left and Bettoni headed home, continuing his promising start to life as a Blue following his move from Wigan Athletic. The Blues reduced the deficit further in the 53rd minute. Watson’s free-kick was blocked and Bettoni’s follow-up also struck a defender, but Richards collected the loose ball and thumped a superb effort into the net from 25 yards. By this point it was all Chelsea and the pressure kept mounting. Gordon drew us level six minutes later, using two sharp touches and his pace following a ball down the channel to beat Josh Briggs before finishing well from the corner of the six-yard box. Olutayo Subuloye went close to putting us ahead in the 68th minute when he rose highest, but none of his team-mates could provide the required finish at the far post. But somewhat against the run of play, West Ham regained the lead with 10 minutes remaining. Freddy Bernal produced an outstanding point-blank save to deny Battrum, but with no offside flag forthcoming, Landers converted the rebound from close range. Calvin Diakite, introduced for Richards, made an immediate impact as he was brought down inside the penalty area in the 87th minute. Watson stepped forward and smashed the resulting spot-kick into the roof of the net. West Ham would have won it themselves had it not been for Bernal making a superb save with his feet from a header in the first minute of added time. Instead, Chelsea completed the turnaround moments later. A defensive error released Ezenwata, who lifted the ball beyond the advancing goalkeeper with the side of his foot. The victory gives us our first three points of the 2026/27 Premier League 2 campaign following the opening defeat at Bournemouth, moving us into the top half of the table. Cobham Next Gen return to PL2 action on Saturday 12 September, when we travel to face Arsenal Under-21s at Meadow Park. Kick-off is at 1pm, and you can watch the game live on CFC+. Chelsea: 1. news.title: How challenges of the past continue to shape Emi Martinez's future
news.body_en: For much of his career, Emi Martinez has been driven by one ambition: to win. And he has built quite the CV: a FIFA World Cup, two Copa Americas, two FIFA Best Goalkeeper of the Year awards, a UEFA Europa League and an FA Cup. That only scratches the surface, too. There’s no shortage of experience. But behind the trophies and accolades is something much deeper. His relentless desire to win and hunger to keep pushing for more can be traced back to his childhood and the sacrifices his parents made to help him chase his dream. He has never forgotten their efforts. And now, as he joins us at Cobham wearing a Chelsea shirt for the first time, he’s more than ready for his next chapter. ‘I like to think about the past,’ Martinez says. ‘I like to see where I’ve come from. It reminds me of the tireless work from my family and me. That's my style. That's how I approach life. ‘I helped my family come from poverty into the life that we have now. My mum and dad worked 15 hours a day to give me this opportunity, and they helped inspire me. Everything today is for them. ‘Chelsea are one of the best clubs in the world, not just in England.  I'm super excited and I wanted that challenge. ‘I attach my life to football. I live for football. I sleep for football. All I care about is having a good family and winning football matches, and now I get to do that for Chelsea.’ That relentless desire for success is something Martinez, who made his debut in our 4-3 victory over Brighton and Hove Albion, believes makes him and the Blues the perfect match. ‘Chelsea and I have a winning mentality,’ he continues. ‘I think we connect in that sense. It’s all about winning. Win or nothing, and I have won everything as an international and as an individual goalkeeper. ‘I’ve been in England for nearly 17 years and now, for me, it's about winning the Premier League. That’s what is missing in my beautiful career. I have come to a club where winning is a priority. And for me, trophies are such a priority. It’s the perfect match.’ The 33-year-old’s role at Chelsea will extend beyond simply keeping the ball out of the net and winning football matches. Having built a reputation as a goalkeeper whose personality and presence can have a significant influence on those in front of him, he wants everyone around him to feel that same confidence from the moment they step onto the pitch. He explains: ‘I want my team-mates to look back and feel, "Oh, Emi's there". I want them to trust me. I want to give them that peace from the back so they can play free. My role is to help them as much as I can. I want to protect them. ‘When you see the Chelsea squad and the size of the club, it just speaks for itself. We’ve got wonderful talent up front, wonderful players at the club, experienced players. So that mix can really help us move forward as a club.’ Martinez is the second player to have swapped Villa Park for Stamford Bridge this summer. Morgan Rogers joined the Blues earlier in the transfer window and the Argentine is looking forward to reuniting with the England international in the Blues dressing room. ‘It’s great to see the likes of Morgan [Rogers] again,’ Martinez smiles. ‘He's such a brilliant talent that I saw coming through from Middlesbrough to Aston Villa. He’s developed so much in his game. And for me, he's the best English forward alongside Cole (Palmer) – the best two English players.’ Martinez has already enjoyed his first experience of Stamford Bridge and the atmosphere created by the Chelsea faithful. Yet there will be much more to come in the months ahead, and he is looking forward to delivering for the Blues supporters. ‘I'm going to give 100 per cent for Chelsea with pride,’ he says. ‘I’m going to try and win games, keep clean sheets, and get Stamford Bridge rocking. ‘It's a huge club, and I won't be happy with draws or losing, so I think I’ll have a connection with the fans. All I want to do is win games.’

news.title: Highlights: Cobham Next Gen 5-4 West Ham U21s
Alonso: 'I’m very happy to feel this energy and support at the Bridge'
news.body_en: As Xabi Alonso took his seat in the Chelsea dugout ahead of our victory over Brighton and Hove Albion, he glanced briefly to the Shed End where a banner had been unfurled in his honour. It read: 'Not too Xabi. Alonso is a Blue' It was a fitting way to mark Alonso's first Premier League home fixture at Stamford Bridge – and the Blues' performance certainly entertained those in the stands. We went ahead inside four minutes when Romeo Lavia prodded home from close range following a corner. Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro then struck to put Alonso's side in a commanding position just after the half-hour mark. Yet Brighton hit back, first through Malick Yalcouye and then via a Joao Pedro own goal. However, after regaining our composure, Cole Palmer expertly guided home a fourth goal to seal the points, despite Pascal Gross scoring late on for the Seagulls. Alonso enjoyed the manner of our victory, although he accepted there are aspects of his side's performance that must be improved. What the Blues manager had universal praise for was the backing from the Chelsea faithful before and during the 90 minutes. ‘It felt great,' he reflected after the Blues' 4-3 victory. 'I’m very happy to come to the Bridge and feel this energy and support. There will be great games, there will be difficult moments, but we need to stick together.’ It was highlighted in Alonso's post-match press conference that the Blues had come away victorious despite having significantly less of the ball than Brighton. When asked if that was by design, the Blues manager reiterated that the demands on his players will adapt to each game. He explained:  ‘You need to have context for the data. For sure, after 30 mins when we scored to make it 3-0, probably in that moment we have played too much with the result [in mind] instead of keeping on playing. 'So, it’s about how we play and what we can do better. I never say we need 60 per cent or 20 per cent possession. It’s about how we prepare and how we can be more competitive. 'You have to adapt, even during games, and there are different moments and there are some moments we’ve done really well and others we can do better.’

news.title: Full Match: Cobham Next Gen vs West Ham U21s
Emi Martinez on taking the Chelsea No.26 shirt: ‘I spoke with John Terry!’
news.body_en: The No.26 shirt made famous at Chelsea by John Terry has a new owner, and Emi Martinez has promised to wear it with pride after joining the Blues from Aston Villa. It was confirmed yesterday (Sunday) morning that Martinez had signed for Chelsea – and he made his debut in our eventful 4-3 victory over Brighton. Martinez made several crucial saves during his first 90 minutes as a Blue, as we made it two wins from two in the Premier League. Ahead of the game at Stamford Bridge, Martinez was announced as our new No.26. He doesn’t take the privilege lightly, with only three other players – and most famously Chelsea legend John Terry – being assigned the squad number in the 21st century. Martinez explained that he had spoken to our former skipper – Terry coached at Aston Villa during the goalkeeper's time in the Midlands – before taking on the famous shirt. He said: ‘I remember using the 26 on loan a few times with previous clubs, and of course I knew John Terry famously had the 26 here. ‘John was someone I spoke to before I joined, and he said he was over the moon to have me here. From our time together at Aston Villa, he knows how hard I work and what I can bring to Chelsea. JT really helped me with my decision. ‘The morning I signed, I texted him and said, "I'm wearing your shirt, and I'm going to do it with pride."'

news.title: A special day for Chelsea and Joao Pedro!
news.body_en: There was a moment at Stamford Bridge where Joao Pedro buried his head in his hands and the Brighton fans behind the goal taunted their former hero. The Brazilian had just dragged an effort wide that you would have put money on him tucking away, especially given the form the forward has been in. But the saying ‘the cream always rises’ couldn’t be more apt, and it wasn’t long before Chelsea's No.9 was celebrating in front of those Seagulls fans situated in the Shed End as he rifled home a low drive into the bottom corner to extend our lead to 3-0. The joy on his face said it all; this goal meant more. However, this is the Premier League, and no game is a given. Our 3-0 advantage – courtesy of goals from Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro – was reduced to 3-1 just before the break. Momentum then shifted. Brighton were pushing and pulled another goal back to make it 3-2, ironically via the boot of Joao Pedro, who diverted a cross his own net. Several fine stops from debutant Emi Martinez kept the visitors at arm’s length before Cole Palmer – who else? – continued his fine form against the Seagulls by putting the game to bed with a stunning strike. So, what did our centre-forward make of all that then? ‘I think we started really well, and we got ourselves into a very commanding position with the three goals,’ Joao Pedro explained. ‘Once we conceded a goal though, it brought Brighton back into the game. ‘I think we should have been more consistent and not allow them to get that energy and belief, because we could have killed the game a lot earlier. ‘But I think the team did really well overall, and Dibu [Emi Martinez] showed his quality with some really good saves. ‘We all tried our best defensively and, step by step, we achieved our level, saw the game out and of course the most important thing was to get the three points, which we did.’ It was another productive afternoon for our new attacking line of Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers – the former two finding the net and the latter causing Fabian Hurzeler’s side a mountain of problems off the left and creating our second goal. Joao Pedro was sharp, led the line expertly and took his goal well – celebrating in front of the Brighton fans who once adored him – and the forward revealed that part of the tactical approach was to utilise the Brazilian’s pace against his former club. ‘I know them [Brighton] really well, so I knew I could be dangerous on the counter and when we turned over possession,’ he stated. ‘We felt that we could show a little bit of speed up front, and we utilised that well. ‘I think up front we are very strong, and myself, Cole and Morgan are linking up well. To be honest, throughout the whole team we have good depth, we have very good players in each position and now we need to build the confidence, the togetherness and maintain this form. ‘It’s been a good start to the season and hopefully we can keep winning.’

news.title: Full match: Chelsea vs Brighton
Inside the life of Katie McCabe
news.body_en:
After providing an assist on her competitive Chelsea debut against Real Sociedad, Katie McCabe fills us in on her journey so far and how she likes to spend her time away from the sport. Could you start by telling us where you grew up and what it was like? I grew up in Tallaght in Dublin. And, yeah, it was amazing; proper old school. There were no phones, so just constantly out on the football pitches playing football with the boys and spending time with my siblings. What age did you start playing football? What was the name of your first grassroots team? Kilnamanagh AFC, you'll have to do your research on that one, though! View this post on Instagram            
How old were you when you first joined an academy? There were no academies, just the boys' team when I was six. What's been your career highlight to date? I think probably qualifying for the World Cup with Ireland in 2023. Who are your best friends in football? I'm lucky; I have a lot. But my best friend, I would say, is Grace Moloney. Could you name your top three favourite players of all time? I've got all these legends appearing in my mind! I love Damien Duff. I loved Niamh Fahey - she also played for Chelsea. And Eden Hazard. What do you like to do away from football? How do you switch off? I like to be with my friends, going out and socialising. And I like to spend time with my dog and my cat. Are you watching any TV series currently? I'm currently in the middle of the Rafa Nadal documentary. If we looked at your Spotify playlist, who's dominating your most played artists of the year? Sonny Fodera and Fisher. They're both DJs. What are your top three holiday destinations, either that you’ve been to or want to visit? I love Ibiza, Majorca and I also love going to Australia. If you had guests over for dinner, what would you cook for them? Tell the fans something they might not know about you... I think all the information about me is out there already! Maybe that I have 11 siblings. What's the best piece of advice you've ever received? Don't get too high with the highs, and don't get too low with the lows. Finally, what does football mean to you? Football is a massive part of my life, but it's not my whole life. And I think as I've gotten older, I've realised that a bit more. I think to get the best out of me from a football point of view, I know I need to have balance off the pitch.

news.title: Extended: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton
Alonso on Martinez: 'He has this aura to influence'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso was happy with the impact Emi Martinez made on his Chelsea debut and believes the goalkeeper’s ‘aura to influence’ will help the Blues throughout the season. The Argentine international's arrival from Aston Villa was confirmed this (Sunday) morning. Martinez signed a three-year contract at Stamford Bridge and went straight into our starting XI for Brighton and Hove Albion's visit. Martinez looked instantly at home and produced several impressive reaction stops throughout our 4-3 victory, which came through goals from Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer. Alonso was not surprised by the ease with which Martinez settled into the Chelsea side, and only expects the goalkeeper's influence to increase going forward. He said: 'Emi is a World Cup winner, is 33 years old, and is very experienced. I spoke with him yesterday (Saturday) and we talked about the game and our team. He felt ready, and I don’t have to tell him many things for him to perform. 'Even today, while a goalkeeper wants to keep a clean sheet, I am happy with his impact. He has been in the building just 48 hours, so now we will have a whole week to prepare for the next one. ‘Day by day, we will feel this presence because he has this charisma, this aura to influence and have a very positive connection with the rest of the team.’

news.title: Match gallery: Blues score four to overcome Seagulls
Xabi Alonso on overcoming Brighton and Moises Caicedo injury
news.body_en: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso emphasised the ‘value’ of this afternoon's 4-3 victory over Brighton and Hove Albion – and provided an update on Moises Caicedo after the midfielder was forced off with an injury in the second half. For 32 minutes of the contest at Stamford Bridge, the Blues were in full control. We opened the scoring early, with Romeo Lavia converting from close range for his first Chelsea goal, before Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro then found the net. Brighton reacted, though. They reduced the deficit before the interval through Malick Yalcouye and pulled another goal back when Joao Pedro turned a cross into the Blues’ net. However, Alonso’s players displayed their resilience to respond and re-establish our advantage, as Cole Palmer curled an excellent shot home from 20 yards. That proved enough to secure all three points, despite a late consolation from Pascal Gross. Alonso once again highlighted that there are improvements for his side to make in the weeks ahead, but he was pleased the Blues had overcome a difficult opponent to make it two wins from two Premier League fixtures at the start of the campaign. ‘All the wins I enjoy a lot, but it was a game that in different moments had different feelings,' Alonso explained in his post-match press conference. 'In the end, we’re happy with the result. We value this win against a very good opponent who have been tough in the last few years. We are happy with that, and there are things and moments that we have done well, but it’s a process to keep on learning and improving. Usually, that is easier with a win.’ The one negative of the afternoon was Caicedo's injury. The Ecuadorian midfielder missed our opening two fixtures of the season but was introduced from the substitutes' bench midway through the second period. However, 13 minutes after coming on, Caicedo was forced off and replaced by Valentin Barco, who helped the Blues get over the line. 'He was cautious to stop and say his feeling wasn’t the best,' Alonso replied when asked about the midfielder's injury after the game. 'We need to assess during the week, but it wasn’t something new.’

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton
Alonso reflects on victory over Brighton
Lavia reacts to his first Chelsea goal!
Match report: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton
news.body_en: Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer were all on target as the Blues made it three wins from three games with an entertaining 4-3 victory over Brighton and Hove Albion. We were once again free-flowing in attack and opened up a three-goal advantage after just 32 minutes. Lavia netted his first Chelsea goal to break the deadlock after four minutes, and both Neto and Joao Pedro found the net with clinical finishes from inside the penalty area. Brighton reduced the deficit before interval via Malick Yalcouye, and grabbed a second just after the hour-mark when Joao Pedro deflected a cross into our net. Yet Alonso's side, as they did against Fulham, showed the right response to pressure and, with 16 minutes to play, Palmer swept home a 20-yard strike. The Seagulls did grab a late third – Pascal Gross heading home – but it proved nothing more than a late consolation. Alonso made seven changes to the side that started our Carabao Cup second-round victory over Luton Town on Thursday Emi Martinez, whose signing was confirmed earlier in the day, started in goal. Wesley Fofana, Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill were the back three, with Neto and Jorrel Hato at wing-back. Lavia was partnered in midfield by Malo Gusto, and the front three was Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro. Before the action got underway, there were touching tributes to two influential Chelsea figures who passed away this summer: our second all-time highest goalscorer, Bobby Tambling, and our former chairman, Ken Bates. Both will be missed. At Fulham on Monday night, the Blues made a rapid start and were ahead inside 35 seconds. Our opener didn't arrive quite as early against the Seagulls, but just four minutes were on the clock. Neto was heavily involved, as the Portugal international won and delivered a corner that Joao Pedro met at the near post. Mats Wieffer got back onto the line to block, but a mix-up with goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen saw the ball fall to Lavia, who nudged a shot over the line for his first Chelsea goal. The Blues were firmly on top. We moved the ball confidently across the pitch and carried a threat whenever we advanced into Brighton's defensive third. And ten minutes after going ahead, we fashioned our second goal of the contest. Rogers was the creator, collecting a Joao Pedro knock-down and forcing his way past Mario Vuskovic. The England international squared the ball into the penalty area, and Neto burst forward to finish beyond Verbruggen. We should have had a third midway through the half, as Neto chased down and brushed aside Ferdi Kadıoglu and played a pass to Joao Pedro. The Brazilian took a touch, which sat down two Brighton defenders, but he guided his finish from 12 yards wide. Martinez, aside from coming to collect a couple of crosses, had little work to do in the opening half-hour. He did have to produce a smart reaction stop, though, when Yalcouye prodded a cross toward goal. Joao Pedro – booed throughout by the supporters of his former club – briefly silenced the away end with a deserved 32nd-minute goal. Hato was instrumental, exchanging passes in our half with Rogers and surging upfield with the ball. Wieffer was unable to keep up with the Dutchman, who fed the ball to Joao Pedro and the Blues' No.9 made no mistake with his finish. Unfortunately, our three-goal advantage was quickly reduced as Brighton pulled a goal back through Yalcouye, who rifled a volley in off the post after Martinez had denied Diego Gomez. Before the interval, each side created one further chance: Rogers came close for the Blues with a shot from distance that flashed past the post, while Gomez headed wide. The second period remained an open affair – perhaps too much for Alonso's liking. Brighton made better use of the space and caused the Blues problems. Many of the Seagulls' chances fell to Gomez. The Paraguayan forward dragged a shot wide before missing a close-range header from a free-kick. It was a chance he should have scored. Our threat remained and Neto did excellently once again to shrug off Kadıoglu and break into the box. His near-post effort was saved and, on the rebound, Rogers whipped a cross into the six-yard box for Palmer, who could only volley over. Martinez's first big save in a Chelsea shirt came soon after, as he reacted excellently to push wide a shot from Gomez. Unfortunately, from the resulting corner, the ball was worked to Pascal Gross, whose pass deflected off Joao Pedro and ended in our net. Alonso soon turned to his bench. Josh Acheampong, Reece James and Moises Caicedo, playing his first minutes of the season, were introduced. The booked Fofana, Lavia and Neto were replaced. Our changes didn't immediately quell the Brighton tide, and Martinez had to save well from a powerful drive from Olivier Boscagli. It was an important moment as, five minutes later, the Blues struck our fourth goal of the game. The goal had shades of our first, as Joao Pedro controlled and laid off a throw-in. This time, Palmer collected the ball, advanced 20 yards, and then curled a shot expertly beyond Verbruggen. Sixteen minutes remained – and the Blues worked hard to see out the contest. We shifted into a 5-4-1 shape, which largely kept Brighton outside our box, and enabled Joao Pedro to lead several counter-attacks, which were often stopped illegally by Brighton defenders. There were five minutes of stoppage time and it appeared there would be no more goals added to the scoreline. However, in the final action of the game, a long Brighton throw was flicked on and headed home by Gross. It proved too late to alter the destination of the points, with Alonso's side taking six from our opening two top-flight fixtures. We travel across London next weekend to face Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday 6 September. Kick-off is scheduled for 4.30pm (UK time). Emiliano Martinez signs for Chelsea!
news.body_en: Chelsea is delighted to announce the signing of Argentinian international Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa. The 33-year-old goalkeeper, who won the World Cup in 2022, has signed a three-year deal with the Blues. 'I’m delighted to be at this football club,' Martinez said. 'Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I’m just over the moon - I can’t wait to get started. 'I want to be successful here. I'm someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it’s a football club that wins titles, so I think it’s a good match. 'I’m all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100 per cent every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.' Having started his career in the youth system of Independiente, Martinez completed a move to Arsenal in August 2010, aged 17. After several loans to gain first-team experience, he became a regular for Arsenal in the 2019/20 campaign, starting the last 11 matches and winning the FA Cup. He won the Community Shield at the start of the following season before signing for Aston Villa in September 2020. During his time in the Midlands, Martinez established himself as one of the world’s leading goalkeepers. He made 256 appearances for Villa across six seasons and lifted the UEFA Europa League in May. Martinez made his international debut in June 2021 and has since been Argentina’s first-choice goalkeeper, earning 67 caps for his country. He has twice won the Copa America (2021 and 2024) with La Albiceleste and lifted the World Cup in 2022. Following those successes, Martinez received the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world’s best-performing goalkeeper, at the 2023 and 2024 Ballon d’Or ceremonies.

news.title: Watch Emi Martinez's first interview as a Chelsea player
news.body_en: England has been home to Emi Martinez for almost 17 years. Yet while the country has shaped him as a person and a player, it is the values instilled while growing up in the Argentine city of Mar del Plata that have underpinned his career. Martinez officially began his journey in the English game – and eventually to becoming a Chelsea player – in August 2010. He had developed a reputation as one of South America's most promising goalkeepers while in the Independiente youth system and earned a move to Arsenal. Far away from home, Martinez had to adapt quickly. Within a year, he had learned English and passed his driving test. Yet on the pitch, it took far longer for the goalkeeper to make his mark. There were several loans in the Football League, and a brief spell in La Liga with Getafe, but as the 2019/20 campaign reached its conclusion, Martinez got a run in the Arsenal first team and never looked back. He lifted the FA Cup and the Community Shield before joining Aston Villa. During Martinez's time in the Midlands, he established himself as Argentina's first-choice goalkeeper and lifted two Copa Americas and a FIFA World Cup. In each of those triumphs, Martinez's drive and determination have shone through. And that mentality was formed in his childhood, as he explained in his first interview since becoming a Blue, which you can watch in full for free above. 'Becoming a footballer was always to help my family, to get them a better life and take them out of poverty,' Martinez explained. 'That drive is still in my football career. It doesn’t matter what I’ve won or where I’ve reached, I want more. 'I want them to be proud of me. Now I’ve got kids, I want them to see nothing comes easy in life. So I am still competing and I want more.’ Martinez has joined the Blues after six seasons at Villa Park, during which he twice received the Yashin Trophy, awarded to the world's best-performing goalkeeper. Now 33 years old, Martinez has no intention of settling on his former glories. He knows the expectations that come with being a Chelsea player and wants to match them throughout his time at Stamford Bridge. ‘I give 100 per cent every game and, when you see me play every day or in training sessions, I give you my all,' he says. 'I try to win every game; it doesn’t matter who we play against. I am bringing that here to this club because it’s a winning club that wins titles and wins things.'

news.title: Alonso: Now is the time to deliver
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso wants to repay the Chelsea supporters for their warm welcome with victory in an early test of our Premier League credentials on home soil against Brighton & Hove Albion. Our new manager has already experienced the support of the home crowd at Stamford Bridge on two occasions, when we beat Real Sociedad in our final friendly of pre-season and then defeated Luton Town to book our place in the Carabao Cup third round on Thursday evening. For the first home Premier League fixture of Alonso’s reign, Brighton are the visitors to west London in a 2pm kick-off on Sunday afternoon, with the Spaniard expecting another good reception for him and his team from the Blues fans. ‘It’s nice,’ responded Alonso. ‘We are happy to have that support and myself to have this welcome from the fans. ‘I have felt since the first day I was here that they were happy that we were starting this time together. Now is the time to deliver and the time to show it every weekend. ‘We’ve had two games and it’s a good start, but it’s still early days. On Sunday, we have a good game, a good test, to see where we are. ‘We will have bumps in the road, for sure, and we need to prepare for that. How we react, how we stick together, how we keep the mentality will be important. ‘So it’s early days and there have been good things, but there are things to develop and progress as well.’ Alonso has faced Brighton’s manager before, during his time at Bayer Leverkusen, leaving the Spaniard expecting a tough but important test of Chelsea’s early season progress from Fabian Hurzeler’s Seagulls side. ‘I know him very well from Germany, from St Pauli,’ added Alonso. ‘He is developing the team with new players. ‘They are a very intense team that do interesting things. So that’s why it’s going to be a good clash and a good test on Sunday.’

news.title: Let's make this our season 🙌
Chelsea vs Brighton: All you need to know
news.body_en: Bank Holiday weekend used to mean Londoners piling onto trains bound for the seaside, but this weekend Brighton & Hove Albion come to Chelsea. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to a 2pm kick-off at Stamford Bridge with Premier League points on the line. Like Fulham away on Monday, this was a fixture the world champions lost last time around after having a player sent off. The 10 men in royal blue led 1-0 but were eventually downed 3-1 with Danny Welbeck, now under Xabi Alonso’s direction, among the visitors’ stoppage-time scorers. In fact the Blues have not beaten the Seagulls since Cole Palmer’s 10-minute hat-trick inspired a 4-2 victory at the Bridge in September 2024. On Thursday the visitors completed the job against Tromso to qualify for the UEFA Conference League proper, only their second European campaign. Last time they had to fulfil European midweeks, in 2023/24, they slipped from the previous sixth-place Premier League finish to 11th. Also on Thursday, Chelsea’s first home game of the season ended in a 2-0 victory over Luton Town, with Welbeck opening his Blues account. The Londoners can now secure three consecutive wins on all fronts for the first time since January (a run of five). Xabi Alonso is hopeful Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo will be ready to face Brighton on Sunday, and confirmed Levi Colwill and Geovany Quenda are in contention to face the Seagulls after missing the win over Luton. 'There were no issues [with Colwill and Quenda], and the plan is that they are training and preparing for the game on Sunday,' said Alonso in his pre-match press conference on Thursday night. 'He [Caicedo] is hopefully training and we are hopeful that he can be involved, but we need to check. No decision has been made.’ One player expected to be in contention to return for the Blues on Sunday is Wesley Fofana, who served the second of his two-match suspension against Luton. Summer signing Jordan Henderson may need more time, with Alonso stating that the Blues are waiting for him to be given the 'green light to play soon' following the injury he sustained during the World Cup. Chelsea have won just one of our past seven first home league games of the campaign, a 3-0 victory over Crystal Palace in 2021 with goals from Marcos Alonso, Christian Pulisic and debutant Trevoh Chalobah's first for the club. The remainder of that run comprises four draws and three losses, but it was not always such hard going at the Bridge. The Blues have won 20 of our previous 34 opening home games in the Premier League era, drawing 10 and losing four. The first of those victories came against Norwich City in 1994, as Glenn Hoddle’s project entered its second season. With the Shed End removed for redevelopment, goals from Frank Sinclair and Paul Furlong either side of the break settled the score. In 1999, a stellar set of goal scorers saw off a decent Sunderland side 4-0 – Gus Poyet (two), Gianfranco Zola and Tore Andre Flo – and a year later Mario Stanic made his mark with a stunning volley during a 4-2 romp against West Ham United. Then, in 2004, the game was forgettable but the result was vital, as Jose Mourinho’s management began with a 1-0 win against title rivals Manchester United thanks to Eidur Gudjohnsen. Three years later, United’s ’noisy neighbours’ Man City were taken apart by goals from iconic trio John Terry, Frank Lampard and Didier Drogba, while in 2010, 1997 FA Cup hero Roberto Di Matteo was shown no mercy as the Blues hit his West Bromwich Albion team for six – a club record for a curtain-raiser at the Bridge. A fine record of opening-day success heralding a title win was upheld in 2016, as Antonio Conte savoured a 2-1 derby defeat of West Ham, ahead of what proved another glorious campaign. Chelsea (1.96) and Brighton (3.54) recorded the highest expected goals tallies over the opening weekend of the Premier League. The Seagulls have scored three goals in each of their past three Premier League encounters with the Blues. Welbeck scored three of those. Following our 3-2 victory at Fulham, Chelsea have won six of the past seven opening away fixtures of the Premier League season. Thanks to Monday’s west London derby win, the world champions are already three points up on last season’s corresponding Premier League fixtures. Victory over Brighton would make that six. Chelsea’s run of 17 league outings without a clean sheet is the longest for the club since the same number in 1991, which ended with the Blues winning 1-0 at Sheffield United on 3 September – straight after a 4-1 home win against Luton Town. Thursday’s 2-0 Carabao Cup victory over Luton was our first shutout in any competition since the 1-0 win in last season’s FA Cup semi-final grudge-match with Leeds United, who will now be our next opponents in the League Cup. Apart from opening his goals account at the first attempt, Morgan Rogers set up five chances for team-mates at Fulham, the most by a Chelsea debutant since the statistic was first recorded in 2003/04. news.title: Danny Welbeck: Brighton reunion will be special
news.body_en: After a long and storied career in the Premier League, Danny Welbeck is well-versed when it comes to facing former clubs, but Sunday’s meeting with Brighton & Hove Albion will still hold extra significance for the Chelsea striker. There is a familiar feel to Sunday’s fixture for Welbeck. A career spent representing several Premier League clubs means the experienced forward has often found himself lining up against former team-mates. That will be the case once more when Chelsea face Brighton this weekend. Yet familiarity will not diminish the significance of the occasion. Brighton remain an important part of Welbeck’s story, making Sunday a fixture he is eagerly anticipating. ‘It’s a special one because Brighton are my former team,’ Welbeck said. ‘Fortunately for me, I’ve played against my old teams quite a lot during my career, so it isn’t anything too new. ‘I’m really looking forward to it and I’m excited to keep pushing on.’ The game will provide another opportunity for Welbeck to build on a smooth start to life at Chelsea. Moving to a new club inevitably brings a period of adjustment, with different surroundings, team-mates and working methods to become accustomed to. However, the forward has felt at home from the moment he arrived at Cobham. He has been grateful for the warmth shown by his new team-mates, the staff and the Chelsea supporters, while the presence of several familiar faces helped make his transition even easier. Throw in a debut goal against Luton Town on Thursday night and it's fair to say Welbeck is enjoying life as a blue. ‘I’ve really enjoyed it and it has been pretty easy for me to settle,’ he explained. ‘It’s such a great group and the staff are very welcoming in and around the training ground. ‘Everybody has been great with me and I’ve been received really well by the fans, so I really appreciate that. ‘It was also nice to know a few familiar faces when I walked through the door, which helped me settle. Now I just want to keep building and improving every single day.’ Welbeck is also enjoying the early stages of working under new manager Xabi Alonso. The Blues are still adapting to Alonso’s methods, with new tactical information being introduced and players returning to the group at different stages following the World Cup and injuries. Welbeck believes patience and hard work will be required as those ideas take shape, but he has been encouraged by the opening weeks and is excited about what lies ahead. ‘It’s been really good and it has been a positive start, but we’re only a couple of games in,’ he added. ‘We have to keep working hard and keep learning the new ideas he is bringing to us. ‘There are a lot of new messages, while some players came back a little later and new players are being integrated and having to settle. But it has been really good up until now and there are really exciting times ahead.’

news.title: Alonso: Acheampong is getting better and better
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso highlighted the recent development of young defender Josh Acheampong, who has started the 2026/27 season in impressive form. The Chelsea Academy graduate was part of the senior squad last season, but has come into his own under Alonso’s guidance, playing every minute of competitive action for our Spanish manager so far. After helping us to make a winning start to the Premier League campaign against Fulham last weekend and book our place in the Carabao Cup third round with a clean-sheet win over Luton Town in midweek, Alonso explained why he has been impressed by the 20-year-old. ‘With Josh, in pre-season we saw that he has been getting better and better,’ said the Chelsea manager, ahead of Sunday’s meeting with Brighton & Hove Albion. ‘For me, when he plays with confidence and aggressiveness, he has a lot of attributes for a modern defender because he can play in different positions, he’s good with the ball, and he understands his role. ‘I’ve seen a progression in these few weeks we have been together and he has played very solid games against Fulham and Luton. We are happy that he is feeling this way and we need to help him. ‘There will be different moments in the season for sure, because we want to have healthy competition in all positions. But Josh is doing well and we’re happy for him, and he is happy as well.’

news.title: Cole Palmer on playing free alongside Morgan Rogers
news.body_en: Cole Palmer has revealed the conversations he had over the summer with Xabi Alonso and Morgan Rogers that helped him feel ready to produce his best on the pitch at Chelsea this season. Our No10 found it difficult to match the brilliant form of his previous two campaigns with the Blues last season, when his efforts were hindered by injury. However, joined in the line-up by old friend and new team-mate Rogers, under the guidance of manager Alonso, he has made a strong start to the 2026/27 Premier League. That was seen when he provided the assist for Joao Pedro to give us the lead just 31 seconds into our league opener, Rogers also getting on the score sheet before Palmer netted the winner himself, in a 3-2 victory over Fulham. ‘I just felt joy, really, and a bit of disbelief, because I didn't think we were going to score that quick,’ admitted Palmer. That win at Craven Cottage was the first glimpse of former Manchester City academy team-mates Palmer and Rogers in competitive action together for Chelsea, combining to provide the creative spark. ‘I think we're two different players,’ Cole added, when asked about that combination with Morgan. ‘He's more physical, more powerful and stuff, and I'm more technical and whatnot. ‘I just told him [when he joined] that he'll make a big difference. We're signing other players as well, so we're going to have a good team and we can do something good.’ As well as new team-mates, Palmer is playing under a new manager, following Alonso’s arrival in the dugout over the summer, and shared the main message he received from the Spaniard. ‘He just said to be free, because he knows what I can do when I feel good and I feel like I can go wherever on the pitch and find areas where I can cause damage. That's what he's told me.’ All of that leaves Palmer confident he can be back at his very best in 2026/27, although he revealed it is the mental impact of playing free of injury which he believes will make the biggest difference. ‘There were many things last season. Mainly just injury, though. It's just like, because you've been injured and then you're going out thinking, “oh, can I do certain things?”, kind of overthinking things. ‘It’s like, you're not doing things that you used to be able to do because previously it would hurt if you did it and whatnot. But I'm over that now.’ The evidence of that is clear on the pitch, after Palmer helped us open the new season with a league win over Fulham before booking our place in the Carabao Cup third round by beating Luton Town on Thursday evening. Next up, Palmer and Rogers will be hoping to combine to great effect again in our first home Premier League game of 2026/27, when we host Brighton & Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge on Sunday.
